articles.title: Mourinho: "I can't hide or try to be what I'm not..."
articles.standfirst: The Portuguese coach spoke on El Chiringuito to analyze his second spell at Real Madrid
articles.summary: The Portuguese coach spoke on El Chiringuito to analyze his second spell at Real Madrid
articles.body:
J osé Mourinho sits down before the media for the first time as Real Madrid coach. The Portuguese faces an interview with Josep Pedrerol on El Chiringuito in which he talks about his arrival at the club, what he expects from this new stage, and everything surrounding one of the most demanding dugouts in the world.

'I’m not coming with a speech of promises or with a list of objectives to guarantee. Mourinho prefers to speak of feelings, responsibility and dreams . And he does so from a position he sums up in one sentence: “I come with everything I have.” From there, the Portuguese lays out what it means for him to take charge of Real Madrid. "I come with the love that Real Madrid awakens in me, with the responsibility that Real Madrid demands, with the excitement of a child who has won nothing... I come with absolutely everything. E this thing about promising things... like was done 20 years ago... I’m not into those stories. If you ask me whether I have dreams... I have dreams ," the Portuguese began. '

"How has Mourinho changed? He gives the answer himself. The Portuguese acknowledges a profound evolution, both personally and professionally, although without giving up what he considers his essence. “I have changed so much. I would say the same DNA, obviously, I cannot hide or try to be what I am not... with much more maturity, less emotional, more controlled” .

The belter from an academy player... and his black eye

Mourinho speaks of an evolution built over the years and, above all, through mistakes. He does not deny his past nor consider that regretting is the way to move forward. "As always, since forever... learning from mistakes... but not regretting this or that because I think that in life regretting something that has happened does not help you at all ".

Experience, for the Portuguese coach, is precisely one of a manager's great tools. “Learning from experiences, yes. This job of being a manager, I think that... the more experience we have... the more ‘déjà vu’ moments appear to you... the more quality you have” . And then comes a much more anecdotal issue, but an inevitable one in the interview: the bruise visible on his face. Mourinho dismisses any speculation with humor and explains its origin. “No, it wasn’t a fight. The bruise I have was from poor Lacosta, a kid from Castilla, who hit me with a ball, I was wearing glasses and it struck me” . And then he joked about it. “But that’s not why he wasn’t called up for the last match.”

A locker room and common sense

Mourinho has found a dressing room with hunger. “I have found a dressing room with a great desire to win as the final product of work” , he explains. He also highlights their predisposition: “A dressing room open to common sense” . He even admits that he has not yet had to show his more aggressive side: “They have protected me from this version that is also mine.”

And he gives a clear example of what he demands of them. “Behavior is impeccable.” For Mourinho, his basic rules are not impositions, but matters of common sense: arriving early, watching their diet, going to the gym to prevent injuries. “ Everything I have asked of them is common sense” , he begins. "Everything I have asked of them as basic, non-negotiable principles, which deep down I have told them I ask of them, is common sense: Saying that you have to come an hour before training, not five minutes before, is common sense . It is today’s football: You have to arrive early, you have to have breakfast monitored by the nutritionist, you have to go to the gym every day to prevent injuries... it is for you. It is for us. Everything I have asked of them is common sense ," he says.

His first spell at Madrid

Mourinho also remembers his first spell at Real Madrid and explains what has changed since then. “I don't know. I don't know if it's that or the responsibility of working for Real Madrid, which is for me a fundamental thing” . The Portuguese makes it clear that he especially enjoys this new opportunity: “This thing of working at Real Madrid, I like it a lot, I really like working for Real Madrid” .

The doubts Rodri has had have created doubts for me too

His personal situation has also changed. In his first spell, he had young children and lived with his wife. Now, with them already grown up and living in London, his day-to-day life is different. “Now they are 29 and 26 and live in London and my wife spends a lot of time with the children” . That is why Valdebebas has become even more his center of operations: “When I leave here at 6 or 7... it is very convenient for me to stay here”.

The second part of the interview begins with Kylian Mbappé. Mourinho does not hold back in his praise for the French forward, whom he describes with a mix of admiration and naturalness: “Mbappé is incredible. He makes me laugh sometimes in training” . The explanation comes immediately: “Because he is too good. He is at a stratospheric level” .

The Portuguese man does avoid, however, getting into evaluating what happened last season. He prefers to look ahead and focuses on the collective responsibility for what happened . “It is not for me to judge or analyze what he did last season. A strange season, a complicated season for everyone. In the end it is always the same story, Arbeloa and Xabi paid the price. Winning or losing is multifactorial .” Mourinho believes that it was not only the coaches or the players who failed: “A lot of people failed last year.” And he makes clear the level of demand he wants to instill in this new stage: “This is the commitment I want” . That is why, when he talks about Mbappé, he prefers to think about what he can contribute now. And he finds a first positive sign even before seeing him compete: “A guy who could have come on August 14 and showed up on the 12th... that already tells me something” .

Mourinho also puts the squad planning on the table and, although he admits that the transfer window is still open, he makes his position clear: “I’m not saying there won’t be any more signings because the market is open, but if you ask me directly whether it is closed for me... yes. It is closed” .

In that context, Rodri appears. The Portuguese coach insists that he does not miss the midfielder because he trusts the solutions he already has in the squad: “No, I don’t miss Rodri, we have solutions, we have quality” . Mourinho also highlights his ability to transform the players at his disposal: “I like to think that I have the ability to improve players.”

"I spoke with him a couple of times and Real Madrid makes him a very good offer. I think there is a very good relationship with City. Without negotiating with City, the club has had contacts with Rodri, it has made him an important offer" . However, the footballer's doubts also ended up generating doubts in Mourinho. "Rodri has had doubts, he has hesitated... and Rodri's doubts have created doubts for me" . And he establishes one of the maxims he wants for the club: "Real Madrid is of such a stature that it cannot have players who think twice about it." Pedrerol then suggests whether Rodri's decision can be interpreted as a victory for Barcelona. Mourinho responds bluntly: "Victories are on the pitch, they are the titles. That is where the victories are."

The coach also spoke about Vinicius and denied having influenced his contract renewal. "No, thanks to me? Vinicius is in love with Real Madrid. I only told him: "Vini, where do you want to go? You’ve been in Brazil and at Madrid, you know what Madrid is when you leave, and it’s not worth it." I think that what he has felt when he has seen the group grow has given him an important feeling," said the Portuguese.

' Mourinho had a conflict with the Brazilian a few months ago , when he sided with Prestianni after the racist abuse of Benfica’s Argentine player in the Champions League: "The answer is simple, Prestianni was my player. And that’s it, there’s no more to discuss; 20 players could come and he was my player. Now Vini knows which side I’m on. The other day when they didn’t award him a penalty I was in the middle of the pitch fighting for him".'

People have to learn how to behave with him, and I'm talking about referees. You can't give a penalty to one player and not to Vinicius, protect one player and not Vinicius. They don't respect him," he says in defense of his player... to whom he also leaves a message : "At the stadium level, one thing is celebrating a goal with your own fans and another is celebrating in front of the opposing fans.

articles.title: Madness for Rodri at Camp Nou
articles.standfirst: Huge ovation from Spotify Camp Nou for the international player
articles.summary: Huge ovation from Spotify Camp Nou for the international player
articles.body:
Rodri has become, for now, the big signing of the summer for Barça. The fans are thrilled with the arrival of the Spanish international and, since he landed in Barcelona on Monday afternoon, he has not stopped receiving displays of affection. This Wednesday, during the squad presentation, he received the biggest ovation of the traditional Joan Gamper Trophy and confirmed that his arrival has sparked enormous excitement among the supporters.

The midfielder was the last player to step onto the pitch during the team presentation, and his appearance prompted the biggest ovation of the afternoon. The decibels soared in the stands of the Spotify Camp Nou when his name was announced, and the footballer responded to the fans' affection by applauding and waving.

Expectations had already become evident an hour earlier, when Rodri stepped onto the pitch to check the state of the playing surface firsthand. At that moment, he was also greeted with a thunderous ovation by the fans who were already in the stands. The Spanish international showed his gratitude and responded to the supporters’ displays of affection.

Since his arrival on Monday afternoon, the new blaugrana player has experienced a true wave of adoration. Many supporters went yesterday to the Spotify Camp Nou offices to try to see him up close and welcome him. The excitement also spread to the exit of the restaurant where Rodri had lunch with members of the Barça board, where he once again received the warmth of the fans.

The excitement over his arrival is even reflected in the streets. Just a few hours after Barcelona made the midfielder's signing official, shirts bearing the name Rodrigo and the number 16 were already being seen around the Spotify Camp Nou .

articles.title: Real Madrid is valued at 2.4 billion and leads world football in brand value: Barcelona, second
articles.standfirst: Real Madrid not only leads in economic value, but also in brand strength
articles.summary: Real Madrid not only leads in economic value, but also in brand strength
articles.body:
Real Madrid retains for the third consecutive year the title of the most valuable and strongest football club brand in the world , with a valuation of 2.4 billion euros , 25% more than the previous year , while Barcelona keeps second place with a value close to 2 billion , according to the "Football 50 2026" report by Brand Finance .

The study also reflects the record growth of the business of football’s biggest brands: the 50 most valuable collectively reach 23.9 billion euros , the largest annual increase since this ranking began to be compiled fifteen years ago. The top ten clubs account for almost two thirds of that value, at 14.9 billion.

The Real Madrid not only leads in economic value, but also in brand strength, with a score of 95.8 out of 100, the highest among the 281 clubs analyzed. The consultancy links this position to the club's international reach, its fan base, its history, the presence of star players, and its ability to turn its sporting prestige into commercial appeal.

The impact of Spotify Camp Nou on Barcelona's 15% growth in value

Barcelona, for its part, remains in second place after increasing its brand value by 15%, bringing it close to 2 billion euros. Brand Finance attributes part of this growth to the return to Spotify Camp Nou after more than two years and to the two consecutive LaLiga titles.

The difference between both Spanish clubs and the rest of world football is once again reflected in the ranking. Arsenal, which makes the biggest jump among the major clubs, rises five places to third position and reaches 1.5 billion euros after increasing its brand value by 28%.

The London club benefits from its return to the top of the Premier League after 22 years and from its presence in the Champions League final.

Bayern Munich is fourth , also with 1.5 billion after growing by 21%, while Paris Saint-Germain retains fifth place. Manchester City, Liverpool and Manchester United occupy the following positions, and Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund round out the "top 10".

Atlético de Madrid rises to eleventh position worldwide

Spanish dominance is not limited to the two giants. Atlético de Madrid rises to eleventh place in the world after increasing its brand value by 22%, while Betis is behind another of the standout advances by climbing five places, to 33rd, with growth of 14%.

Athletic Club also appears among the 50 most valuable brands, in 39th place; Villarreal, in 45th; and Real Sociedad, which rounds out the ranking in 50th place.

LaLiga remains the second-strongest football league brand in the world

In the realm of national competitions, LaLiga remains the second strongest football league brand in the world, behind only the Premier League and ahead of the Bundesliga, Serie A, and Ligue 1.

The consulting firm believes that the challenge for Spanish football now lies in leveraging the international profile of Real Madrid and Barcelona to strengthen the value of the other clubs and LaLiga itself, especially with the 2030 World Cup on the horizon, to be hosted by Spain, Portugal, and Morocco together with Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

articles.title: Diomande: "I am ready to die for Mourinho"
articles.standfirst: The new Real Madrid player has spoken for the first time as a Los Blancos player for Sporty TV
articles.summary: The new Real Madrid player has spoken for the first time as a Los Blancos player for Sporty TV
articles.body:
Yan Diomande, Real Madrid's star signing this summer, has given an interview to SportyTV in which he spoke about how his transfer came about, what José Mourinho's call was like, and explains the advice he received from Didier Drogba after learning of his arrival at the white club.

The player says he is "proud and happy because I have made my dream come true". His goal has always been to be the best player in the world and he is still pursuing it. He considers himself humble, but "confident in himself".

His reaction to the signing

'He will never forget his reaction when he found out that Madrid wanted to sign him: "It was like a dream because there is no bigger club. From the moment I found out, I couldn't sleep. I couldn't believe it. I spoke with Juni and then I spoke with the coach. I was surprised because he spoke French. Mourinho got up at 5 in the morning to talk to me. That means he is important. When Madrid calls you, you can't say no, so I said: "If they want me, that's where I'll be."'"

Also remember what Mou’s first words were: "As soon as I arrived, he told me: "I promised you that you were going to be part of my team, and here you are." And I told him: "I’m happy to work with you because you are the best." I can learn a lot from him; he is the right coach to continue my development. I am prepared to die for him".

His connection with Leganés

It is curious to remember that Diomande made his professional debut against Madrid at the Bernabéu: "It is God's doing. I believe a lot in God. And it has been quite a coincidence. I just want to enjoy every day. From that match I remember swapping shirts with Mbappé, and today we are in the same dressing room laughing together. I will never forget Leganés because it was the only club that gave me the opportunity to show my quality".

articles.title: The Messi vs Cristiano Ronaldo duel continues in a jersey auction. Which sold for six times more than the other?
articles.standfirst: A personal moment with Messi helped make his Barcelona jersey one of soccer's most valuable collectibles
articles.summary: A personal moment with Messi helped make his Barcelona jersey one of soccer's most valuable collectibles
articles.body:
The rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo has produced countless debates over who stands above the other, but the latest comparison between soccer's two icons came in a very different arena.

A shirt worn by Messi during Barcelona ’s 2012 pre-season friendly against Manchester United has sold for $66,107 at auction, comfortably surpassing a Ronaldo jersey from his Real Madrid career that attracted a $10,601 bid.

Both items came from the personal collection of former Manchester United masseur Rod Thornley , who spent years working closely with some of the biggest names in soccer during his time at the club.

The huge difference in price was largely driven by the unique story behind Messi ’s shirt, which wasn't simply collected after the match but personally handed over by the Argentine superstar himself.

How Rod Thornley secured Messi’s unforgettable shirt

The connection between Thornley and the Messi jersey dates back to Barcelona’s goalless draw with Manchester United in August 2012.

Knowing the opportunity to secure a shirt from one of soccer’s greatest-ever players was special, Thornley reached out to former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique before the game.

“I messaged Gerard Pique a couple of days before the game and said, ‘I never ask you for anything, but I need Messi’s shirt from this one,’” Thornley explained.

“At the end of the game Gerard came into our dressing room, grabbed me, and walked me straight into theirs. Messi still had the shirt on his back.”

The moment became even more memorable when Messi personally removed the shirt, signed it and handed it over: “He took it off, signed it to me while I sat there with him, and shook my hand. It was incredible.”

That personal interaction helped make the shirt one of the most valuable pieces from the collection.

Ronaldo and Giggs shirts also attract major bids

The Cristiano Ronaldo shirt included in the auction came from the Portuguese forward’s Real Madrid era during the 2014-15 season.

Unlike the Messi jersey, it was a match-issued shirt rather than one confirmed to have been worn during a game. It also featured a personal message connected to Thornley , who had worked with Ronaldo during his first spell at Manchester United .

While the jersey attracted significant interest, it fell well short of the price achieved by Messi ’s shirt.

The auction also featured other pieces of Manchester United history, including a match-worn shirt belonging to Ryan Giggs from the club’s famous 4-0 Champions League victory over Olympiacos in 2002. That shirt sold for $10,103.

The auction result added another fascinating chapter to the careers of two players whose legacies continue to generate headlines long after their greatest battles on the pitch.

A shirt worn by Messi during Barcelona ’s 2012 pre-season friendly against Manchester United has sold for $66,107 at auction, comfortably surpassing a Ronaldo jersey from his Real Madrid career that attracted a $10,601 bid.
Both items came from the personal collection of former Manchester United masseur Rod Thornley , who spent years working closely with some of the biggest names in soccer during his time at the club.
The huge difference in price was largely driven by the unique story behind Messi ’s shirt, which wasn't simply collected after the match but personally handed over by the Argentine superstar himself.
How Rod Thornley secured Messi’s unforgettable shirt
The connection between Thornley and the Messi jersey dates back to Barcelona’s goalless draw with Manchester United in August 2012.
Knowing the opportunity to secure a shirt from one of soccer’s greatest-ever players was special, Thornley reached out to former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique before the game.
“I messaged Gerard Pique a couple of days before the game and said, ‘I never ask you for anything, but I need Messi’s shirt from this one,’” Thornley explained.
“At the end of the game Gerard came into our dressing room, grabbed me, and walked me straight into theirs. Messi still had the shirt on his back.”

The moment became even more memorable when Messi personally removed the shirt, signed it and handed it over: “He took it off, signed it to me while I sat there with him, and shook my hand. It was incredible.”
That personal interaction helped make the shirt one of the most valuable pieces from the collection.

The Cristiano Ronaldo shirt included in the auction came from the Portuguese forward’s Real Madrid era during the 2014-15 season.

articles.title: Miguel Ángel Gil: "We are going to help Julián; we need him to compete among the big clubs"
articles.standfirst: Atlético's CEO definitively rules out the possible departure of the Argentinean
articles.summary: Atlético's CEO definitively rules out the possible departure of the Argentinean
articles.body:
The Julián Alvarez saga is over, if it hadn't already been settled for months. Miguel Ángel Gil , Atlético's CEO, has definitively put an end to the possible departure of the Argentine striker with statements to the EFE news agency. La Araña has been one of the names of the summer. The footballer who has taken up the most space in radio talk shows, television programs, sports websites and newspaper pages. It's over. La Araña will continue wearing Atlético's shirt.

Atlético de Madrid's CEO insisted to EFE this Friday on Julián Alvarez's continuity in the team and stressed that the red-and-white club is going to "help" the forward and will "continue taking care of him" so that he can give "his full potential," and stressed that they need him "to keep competing among the greats of Europe."

Miguel Ángel Gil wanted to settle the debate over Julián's future once again. The club's CEO had already spoken about this matter very forcefully last July 17. A month later, he again confirms what was said at that time. "Atlético de Madrid, like all the big clubs, is built with great players and I am certain that Julián is one, as well as a great professional. We must compete with our values, with people from the club and with the best players from outside that we can bring in" , he stated.

We cannot allow other clubs and their allied media to decide what we have to do, dictate our sporting strategy, and disrespect us

After months with the footballer's situation on everyone's lips, Miguel Ángel referred to the player's immediate future and Atlético's role.

"We are going to help Julián and we are going to keep looking after him so that he can give us his full potential, because we need him to keep competing among the giants of Europe. We must understand that Julián has not had the best advisers close to him regarding his professional career in recent months ," he warned.

Atlético de Madrid, like all the great clubs, is built with great players and I am certain that Julián is one of them, in addition to being a great professional. We must compete with our values, with homegrown people and with the best players from outside that we can bring in

And he also added a clear message for FC Barcelona. "We cannot allow other clubs and their allied media to decide what we have to do, set our sporting strategy, and disrespect us" .

"That is precisely what they are looking for: to divide us. It is clear that we are not as powerful as they are, but we have values . We Atlético supporters are not going to allow them to contaminate us. Atleti is strong when we are all together," Miguel Ángel Gil stressed.

Atlético de Madrid has been very clear about Julián's situation for months. The red-and-white club maintains the same initial stance and has no intention of transferring the Argentine footballer, who continues to work normally under Cholo's orders and could be called up to face Villarreal next Sunday. The club points to his release clause and his contract to rule out any departure, whether to Barcelona or Arsenal. For Atlético there is no further debate, Julián is staying with the red-and-white side.

articles.title: Mourinho has winning start at Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: A typical Joselu goal decided a closely contested match, with Madrid looking very much like last year's team and Espanyol well organized. Arda, the standout player, was substituted. Bellingham and Calatrava scored the goals
articles.summary: A typical Joselu goal decided a closely contested match, with Madrid looking very much like last year's team and Espanyol well organized. Arda, the standout player, was substituted. Bellingham and Calatrava scored the goals
articles.body:
Carlos Espí came off the bench to score a late winner for Madrid on his debut for the Spanish giant.

The 21-year-old Espí was one of the standouts of La Liga last season and Madrid reportedly paid Levante 25 million euros ($28 million) for him.

Espí was brought on in the 79th minute and scored 11 minutes later, pouncing after Kylian Mbappé had been knocked off the ball and firing past Marko Dmitrovic.

Jude Bellingham headed in a free kick in the ninth minute and almost scored in similar fashion early in the second half but saw his header fingertipped onto the crossbar by Dmitrovic.

Álex Calatrava had scored a deserved equalizer for the Espanyol in the 30th minute, sweeping the ball past Thibaut Courtois for his first La Liga goal.

Mourinho was hired in June and officially took over in July at the start of the preseason.

He is back for a second stint with Madrid some 13 years after he left the club. He was in charge from 2010-13, winning a Spanish league and a Copa del Rey.

It was Madrid's first match of the season as they and defending champion Barcelona sat out the first weekend because they had players return later from the World Cup.

articles.title: The Metropolitano welcomes Julián Álvarez with whistles
articles.standfirst: The Argentine will start the match on the bench
articles.summary: The Argentine will start the match on the bench
articles.body:
It was the name of the day. Julián Alvarez was returning to the Metropolitano and the fans' verdict was swift. When his name was announced over the stadium loudspeakers, the booing was deafening. La Araña, who had monopolized all the spotlight in the build-up, was also a negative protagonist before the match kicked off. The rojiblanco supporters made their displeasure clear with the attitude of the Argentine player throughout the summer, including a transfer request.

One by one, the names of all the players appeared as the announcer called them over the stadium loudspeakers. The applause followed one after another until Julián’s name appeared. At that moment, the Metropolitano responded with a loud chorus of boos for the red-and-white number 19. In that way, La Araña saw for himself the anger of a fanbase that had been expecting a gesture from him before he put on the Atlético shirt again. That did not happen.

To briefly summarize how events unfolded over these past months, last May 25 MARCA broke the soap opera of the summer: Julián Alvarez sat down with Atlético’s executives to tell them that his dream and wish was to continue his career playing for Barça. Thus began a very tough summer for the red-and-white supporters . Just a few weeks later, during the World Cup, the striker spoke out. It was the early hours of June 23, and the football world came to a standstill because of Julián’s statements.

“The truth is that I don’t know. It’s not the time to talk about this, but I can’t hide either or pretend nothing’s going on. Honestly, I try to be an honest person and I spoke with the people at the club I needed to speak with. I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer and to fulfill my dream,” a nervous Julián Álvarez said. After those statements, it would be Miguel Ángel Gil’s turn. The Atlético CEO made it clear time and again, on three separate occasions, that Julián was not going to leave the red-and-white club. Today, he has had to face his fans after months of tension.

articles.title: Where should Julián Alvarez go next? The best landing spot after his Atlético Madrid fallout
articles.standfirst: The Argentinian forward has experienced months of frustration and wants to play for another club
articles.summary: The Argentinian forward has experienced months of frustration and wants to play for another club
articles.body:
The relationship between Julián Alvarez and Atlético Madrid appears to be reaching a breaking point. The transfer rumors have now evolved into one of the biggest stories of the European soccer summer. On Sunday, the tension became impossible to ignore when Atlético supporters loudly booed the Argentine forward before their La Liga match against Villarreal.

For a player who arrived as one of the club's marquee stars, it was a stunning turn of events. The boos were not subtle. When Alvarez's name was announced over the stadium loudspeakers at the Metropolitano , supporters responded with a chorus of whistles and jeers. The reaction reflected months of frustration after the World Cup-winning striker reportedly informed club executives that his dream was to continue his career with Barcelona.

Alvarez later acknowledged the situation publicly. “The truth is that I don't know. It's not the time to talk about this, but I can't hide either or pretend nothing's going on,” he said during the summer. “Honestly, I try to be an honest person and I spoke with the people at the club I needed to speak with. I think the best thing for everyone is a transfer and to fulfill my dream.”

Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil r epeatedly insisted the player would not be sold, but the situation has only become more uncomfortable. After the 2-2 draw with Villarreal, manager Diego Simeone revealed that club officials instructed Alvarez to head directly to the dressing room rather than join teammates in greeting supporters after the match.

At this point, even if a transfer does not happen immediately, the relationship between player and fan base appears badly damaged. That raises an important question: if Alvarez does leave Atlético Madrid, where should he go?

Barcelona remains the dream move

The most obvious answer is the one Alvarez himself has already identified. Barcelona makes sense from both a football and personal perspective. The Argentine has reportedly made no secret of his admiration for the Catalan giants , and his technical style appears tailor-made for the club's possession-based approach. At 26 years old, Alvarez is entering the prime of his career. Barcelona could offer him the opportunity to become one of the central figures of a project built around young stars and attacking football.

His versatility would also be a major asset. Julian can operate as a traditional striker, a second forward, or even in wider attacking roles. That flexibility would give Barcelona numerous tactical options. The challenge, of course, is financial. The Culés' well-documented economic constraints could make a deal difficult, especially if Atlético remains determined not to strengthen a direct domestic rival.

Arsenal could be the Premier League's perfect fit

If Barcelona cannot make the numbers work, Arsenal may be the most intriguing alternative. The Gunners have spent recent seasons building one of Europe's most exciting squads , but many observers still believe they need another elite finisher to take the final step toward winning major trophies consistently. Alvarez's relentless work rate , pressing ability, and finishing quality would fit perfectly into Mikel Arteta's system.

Unlike some traditional No. 9s, Julian contributes heavily without the ball, making him an ideal match for Arsenal's high-energy style. He would also reunite with a league where he previously thrived during his time at Manchester City. A move to North London could offer Alvarez the chance to become the undisputed centerpiece of an attack while competing for Premier League and Champions League titles.

Liverpool would be a dangerous option

Liverpool should also be considered among the strongest possibilities. The club has a long history of maximizing versatile attacking players, and Alvarez possesses many of the qualities that have traditionally flourished at Anfield.

His movement, pressing intensity, and ability to create goals as well as score them would fit seamlessly into Liverpool's attacking structure. From a sporting perspective, Liverpool could offer something that Atlético currently cannot: a fresh start without the baggage of a fractured relationship between player and supporters.

Why Staying at Atlético looks increasingly difficult

The reality is that repairing the current situation may be harder than finding a new club. Atlético fans have always embraced players who fully commit to the badge and Simeone's demanding culture. Once supporters believe a player wants to leave, rebuilding trust can be an uphill battle.

Sunday's reaction at the Metropolitano demonstrated just how much frustration has accumulated. The boos were not directed at Alvarez's performances on the field. They were directed at a player many supporters feel has already decided his future lies elsewhere. Even if Atlético refuses to sell him this summer, every home match could become another chapter in a saga that distracts both the player and the club.

Several elite clubs could benefit from adding Alvarez. Arsenal would gain a complete forward capable of elevating an already talented attack. Liverpool would acquire one of the world's most versatile offensive players. Other European giants would undoubtedly line up if he became available. But if the question is which destination makes the most sense, the answer remains Barcelona.

articles.title: A stunning offensive display by Barcelona against Elche
articles.standfirst: Hansi Flick’s team scored five goals to begin their LaLiga campaign in the best possible way.
articles.summary: Hansi Flick’s team scored five goals to begin their LaLiga campaign in the best possible way.
articles.body:
Barcelona began its LaLiga title defense in dominant fashion with a 5-0 victory over Elche , as the Blaugrana side showcased its attacking firepower despite being without a traditional center forward.

Raphinha, who scored twice, Fermín López , who also netted a brace, and Karim Adeyemi were responsible for the rout delivered by Hansi Flick ’s team, which made a strong statement against an opponent that showed courage and ambition but lacked cutting edge in attack and struggled defensively.

Anselmi’s side, still a work in progress, stepped onto the pitch without fear and willing to challenge the champions for possession. With Barcelona missing several key players and Raphinha operating as a false No. 9, Elche opted for a high press and looked to attack through the wings.

However, Elche’s aggressive approach also left spaces that Barcelona exploited with quick counterattacks. Lamine Yamal delivered the first warning with a run behind the defense, but his effort sailed over the crossbar.

The opening goal came in the 13th minute. A mistake by Elche while playing out from the back allowed Fermín López to set up Raphinha, who was brought down inside the box by Chust as he prepared to shoot. The Brazilian stepped up and converted the penalty to put Barcelona ahead.

The goal did not change Elche’s approach, as the home side continued trying to build from the back and find spaces out wide. Barcelona, meanwhile, began to lose some accuracy and intensity, although Elche created little danger aside from a wayward effort from Ali Houary.

Gavi’s injury forced Flick into an early change before halftime, with Pedri coming on and bringing balance and control back to Barcelona’s midfield. Shortly after, another turnover in Elche’s half allowed Raphinha to assist Adeyemi, who scored his first LaLiga goal to extend Barcelona’s lead before the break.

Barcelona came out in the second half determined to put the match away. Raphinha had a golden opportunity after a brilliant assist from Lamine Yamal, but he failed to convert.

With Pedri dictating play, Flick’s team grew more comfortable as Elche began to run out of energy to maintain its pressing intensity. The champions controlled the match and found their third goal through Raphinha once again, as the Brazilian completed his brace after a pass from Gordon.

Elche tried to fight back and came close to scoring. Buonanotte hit the post, and shortly afterward Joan García denied him in a one-on-one situation with a superb save.

But Barcelona responded immediately. Gordon once again used his pace to get behind Elche’s defense and assisted Fermín López, who scored the 4-0 goal and capped off a brilliant performance with his second strike in the 79th minute.

With an attacking masterclass and a commanding display, Barcelona opened the season by sending a clear message: they are ready to defend their LaLiga crown.

articles.title: The Real Madrid player who makes a last attempt to avoid surgery
articles.standfirst: The Spanish center-back overcomes the muscle problem, but the tibia is struck again: last attempt before the operating room
articles.summary: The Spanish center-back overcomes the muscle problem, but the tibia is struck again: last attempt before the operating room
articles.body:
Raúl Asencio faces one last attempt to avoid surgery. The Real Madrid center-back has already overcome the injury that kept him sidelined this season due to a quadriceps problem , but the same leg is causing him trouble again. This time, in the tibia. An ailment he has been carrying since last season and that did not fully heal as expected .

The situation forces the player to start a new treatment. Asencio has already completed several sessions in Valdebebas with the aim of relieving and recovering the affected area . If the progress is not as expected, the alternative will be to undergo surgery and face an estimated absence of between six and eight weeks.

Last attempt before the operating room

The problem goes back a long way . The tibia already affected the final stretch of last season, when injuries were hitting the Real Madrid squad especially hard. At that time, Asencio decided not to stop . The team needed center-backs and he stepped up even though the risk was obvious. "I'm not stopping now, no way" , he even said when the possibility of stopping was raised. A decision as brave as it was risky, because the player put his body on the line at a time when the team was going through an extreme situation .

The solution then was to look for a middle path that would allow him to keep competing. Asencio underwent a minimally invasive treatment aimed at removing abnormal cells in the area of the tibia scar , where a poorly healed callus had formed. The healing was not adequate and could end up weakening the bone to the point of turning the fissure into a fracture . The medical staff then opted for a treatment that would buy time and avoid immediate surgery. Asencio was able to continue helping the team.

The rest did not close the wound

With the end of the season, it was time to rest. The plan during the summer was simple: rest, recovery, and let the passage of time allow the area to heal . The expectation was that the tibia would respond to the rest after months of strain. But that has not happened. Asencio's situation has worsened and the tibia has once again become a threat to his season . The problem may have been aggravated by the quadriceps injury, also in the same leg, which has forced him to modify his workload and his training during the preseason .

Now the player faces one last attempt before making a much more drastic decision . The treatment is already underway in Valdebebas and the first sessions have already been completed. The aim is to unload the area and get it to respond without the need for surgery. The margin, however, is slim. If the treatment does not work, Asencio will have to undergo surgery and would be out of action for around two months . An especially hard blow for the center-back at the start of a season in which Mourinho cannot count on his entire defense.

articles.title: Mourinho, all the way with Vinicius
articles.standfirst: The Portuguese coach defended Madrid's number 7 in public... and also in private with a conversation in which he wanted to show him his blind trust
articles.summary: The Portuguese coach defended Madrid's number 7 in public... and also in private with a conversation in which he wanted to show him his blind trust
articles.body:
M ourinho has chosen sides. And it is Vinicius 's. The Portuguese coach not only came out publicly in defense of the Brazilian after the match against Espanyol . He also spoke with him in private to convey an unmistakable message: He is and always will be with him . The Brazilian star, recently renewed by Madrid, has barely started working with Mourinho in this new stage, but he already knows that he has the coach on his side as a bulletproof shield.

First I go at him, now you go at him; now I go at him, now you go at him. If I get a yellow, you go at him. I come off, since I have a yellow, someone without a yellow comes on and goes at him

The match in Cornellà does not change that assessment. Vinicius did not have his best night; he was too focused on confrontations with the opponents , he received a yellow card and ended up falling into a dynamic that Mourinho wants to help him control . But a performance below expectations does not alter the coach’s evaluation. Much less after just one match. The Portuguese coach also understands that Vinicius needs to feel supported in a context in which he is once again at the center of everyone’s attention . The boos, whistles and insults he received during the match against Espanyol were constant and the coach did not want to miss the chance to publicly defend his player .

Bulletproof shield.. and a private conversation

“Vini is not a saint, but what they do to him is too much” , Mourinho said. And he went even further by denouncing a situation that, in his view, keeps repeating itself with the Brazilian: “ There is already a pattern, there is something that is repeated among opponents . First I hit him, now you hit him; now I hit him, now you hit him. If I get a yellow card, then you hit him. I go off, because I have a yellow card, and someone without a yellow card comes on and hits him. It is a frustration for him” . The Portuguese also spoke of “bullying” from the stands and from opponents: “We are in a social era of antibullying; with Vini we are still in the bullying of the opponent and the crowd” .

It was not a defense intended to justify everything the Brazilian does. Mourinho knows that Vinicius has to control his emotions and prevent provocations from taking him out of the game . But it is one thing to demand that he improve in that area and quite another to question his importance. Mourinho has no doubts whatsoever about Vinicius. And he wanted the player to know that privately as well.

After the criticism that appeared following the league opener, the coach spoke with him to convey calm and confidence. For Mourinho, Vinicius is a fundamental piece of the team he is building because he needs footballers capable of changing games. Wingers who are not afraid to receive the ball out wide, take defenders on, attack the full-back and force an entire defense to retreat . Vinicius fits that description perfectly. His movement creates space for Mbappé, Bellingham and the rest of the attackers . And his ability to play in open space turns any recovery into a threat.

Mourinho is clear about who he wants

But there is something else that Mourinho especially values: character. The Portuguese coach wants a competitive, aggressive, ambitious Madrid . A team that is not satisfied. And he understands that Vinicius represents a good part of that DNA . His personality, his hunger, his ability to take on responsibility and his obsession with being decisive are part of the characteristics that Mourinho intends to enhance, not extinguish .

That is why the coach does not interpret Vini's first match as a warning sign. On the contrary. He knows that the season has only just begun, that the Brazilian still has room to improve physically and that his performance will grow as his minutes, confidence, and understanding with his teammates increase . The question, for Mourinho, is not whether Vinicius is going to be important. The question is how far he can take him. One of the Portuguese's great missions this season will be precisely that: to maximize his footballers' virtues and get them to reach an even higher level. And with Vini, the challenge is especially appealing.
